# dsh-notification-bridge — Local macOS notification bridge
English | 中文
An independent DSH host plugin, `dsh-notification-bridge`, that does not modify DSH source, preload,
signatures, or internal IPC. Its native Swift Helper is the plugin's delivery backend, not a DSH fo
gnatures, or internal IPC. Its native Swift Helper is the plugin's delivery backend, not a DSH fork.
Repository metadata: `https://github.com/fegnze/dsh-notification-bridge`. The source retains the MyS
pace root repository's Zlib license; see `LICENSE` for a copy. Local DSH icons and signed artifacts
are not distributed. The npm allowlist includes the entry point, client, native source, build/CLI sc
ripts, and English/Chinese READMEs; it excludes locally signed apps, copied DSH icons, tests, and pr
ivate notification queues.
## DSH compatibility
DSH integration is declared only for **0.2.0-rc.2 or 0.2.1-rc.2**. `engines.dsh` and the optional pe
er `@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot` both use exactly `0.2.0-rc.2 || 0.2.1-rc.2`. The optional peer descri
bes the host without installing another DSH runtime; it does not broaden support to later prerelease
s. Recheck the `session/event`, `agent/status`, and `agent/disposed` contracts after upgrading DSH.
Local adapter tests do not replace live session or native-notification acceptance.
## Identity and boundaries
- Native component: `~/Applications/MySpace Notifications.app`, bundle ID `local.myspace.notificatio

ns`; no persistent menu-bar or Dock icon.
- Uses AppKit + UserNotifications under the MySpace Notifi
cations identity, without impersonating DSH's bundle ID. The build copies the icon from the local DS

H installation; the icon binary is not checked in.
- Local ad-hoc signing only: no Apple developer a

ccount, Developer ID, notarization, or public distribution process.
- `accepted: true` only means th
e system API accepted the request; it does not guarantee a banner while Do Not Disturb is active. Ba

nners, icons, and click behavior require visual inspection on a real machine.
- Clicking `open-dsh`
opens `/Applications/DeepSeek Harness.app`; it does not promise to navigate to a specific session. A
rbitrary URLs, shell commands, and executables are not accepted as click actions.
## Build, install, and authorize
Requires the local Xcode Swift compiler and Bun:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Authorization status uses Apple's enum: 0 not determined, 1 denied, 2 authorized, 3 provisional. If
denied, enable it in System Settings → Notifications → MySpace Notifications; authorization is never
bypassed. Occasionally the authorize callback reports an error while a later status is already 2; u
se status and an actual send result as the evidence.
The Helper starts on demand through `open -g`, without installing a LaunchAgent or registering a dae
mon. It runs as an accessory app and keeps notification-click handling available; while normally idl
e, it checks the private queue every 250 ms. Quit MySpace Notifications through Activity Monitor to
stop it; the next send starts it again.
## DSH integration
Declare a local link in the profile's dependencies:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Replace the example absolute path with your actual workspace. The Cordis component ID remains `myspa
ce-notification-bridge`; the service name `myspaceNotifications`, configuration fields, native bundl
e ID, and queue path remain unchanged to preserve existing settings and notification permissions.
Append the package name to `dsh.profile.bundles`, install dependencies for that profile, then reopen
the DSH instance hosting it. Electron exclusively owns the desktop profile, so do not use `dsh plug
in --profile desktop`; do not restart the application while it is hosting an active session.
`sessionEvents: true` is the default: it notifies for root-session completion, failure, stop, limits
reached, blocking, and waiting on ask_user_question; subagents do not generate notifications. Event
s of the same type in the same session are deduplicated within 10 seconds. Set `sessionEvents: false
` in the profile patch to expose only the general-purpose capability. You can disable the dsh-notify
bundle to avoid duplicates; notifications from other plugins must be checked separately and are not
disabled automatically.
Session notification bodies do not show session IDs. They prefer the existing session title (also re
adable from logs after a restart), then a summary of the latest user message, then “当前任务” (“Current
task”). Whitespace in the subject is collapsed and the subject is limited to 100 characters. IDs are
used only for internal deduplication.
Other host plugins declare their dependency through the Cordis service contract:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The service provides `send()` and `status()`. Name/field limits and validation are in `src/client.js
`. Rejection and timeout throw errors; there is no silent AppleScript fallback. Currently this is a
host-only interface, with no HTTP endpoint, browser interface, or MCP tool.
## Non-DSH callers and Butler
Local JS/Bun programs can import `send()` from `src/client.js` or use the CLI. The stdin entry point
keeps notification text out of process argv:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Butler configures the `notification.command` argument array in `butler.json` at its working-director
y root. The Butler host inside the DSH App spawns the command and writes JSON to stdin; it neither i
mports this plugin nor embeds workspace paths. With native transport configured, failures produce wa
rnings rather than falling back to Script Editor notifications. Without a configured command, the ho
st uses the system notification channel.
## Private queue and failure semantics
Uses the current user's `~/Library/Application Support/MySpaceNotifications`: directory mode 0700, r
equest/response mode 0600, UUID filenames, and atomic submission; no TCP port is opened. Same-user p
rocesses are the trust boundary; this does not defend against programs already controlling that user
. The client cleans up after waiting for a response. A timeout removes unconsumed requests, but a no
tification may still arrive if the Helper already accepted the request; neither recall nor exactly-o
nce delivery is guaranteed. The Helper removes expired queue files, and notification bodies are not
written to long-term logs.
